probe: two of 06 §13.1's approximations, settled by running the corpus generator's own output format
method: claude -p --output-format json in a throwaway directory. No plugin, no logger; the point was what the headless result document carries.

sub_to_sub.question: 06 §13.1 item 7: is there now a way to tell a nested subagent from a sibling? P7 found none in the hook payload and the spec says to delete the value if none appears.
sub_to_sub.run: a prompt asking the main thread to spawn a subagent which itself spawns another
sub_to_sub.finding: Nesting IS observable - at session level, in the headless result document, not in the hook payload. P7's conclusion still holds for the hook. max_depth and spawned_by_subagents say whether nesting happened and how much; they do not say WHICH SubagentStop record was the nested one.

tokens_output.question: 06 §13.1 item 6: how far is the char/2.5 estimate from actual usage?
tokens_output.note: usage.output_tokens INCLUDES thinking tokens. Comparing it to the visible reply without subtracting output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens makes the estimate look far worse than it is; that subtraction is what reconciles the three samples.
tokens_output.finding: Korean prose runs at about 1.03 tokens per character, consistently across the three samples once thinking is excluded. The spec's chars/2.5 assumes 0.4 tokens per character - it understates by roughly 2.6x. Ground truth is available in the corpus generator's own JSON (usage.output_tokens minus thinking), so era 02 does not need to estimate at all for its own corpus.

samples_by_content.note: Added after an independent check found the first three samples were all pure Korean prose. The characters-per-token ratio is strongly content-dependent, so a single divisor cannot serve.
samples_by_content.finding: 0.87 to 3.51 chars per token, a 4x range. The spec's 2.5 is close for code (2.78) and English (3.51) and wrong by about -60% for Korean prose (0.97). It was a compromise for mixed content, not a bad guess - but a compromise that is worst on exactly the content this project measures.

fitted_fallback.caveat: Six samples, two parameters, fitted in-sample. The structure (Hangul tokenises about 4x denser than Latin) is a real property; the constants are not settled.
